title: Book Three · Chapter 165: The Four Drawings
story:
Ten days after Anna sends her request, the design school's packet arrives.

She brings it to the library after lessons. Ronan is finishing a school task at the next table.

The school asks for a form and four drawing copies. Two must show the same small building: one from the front and one from above. Another must show a stair. The last is her own choice.

Anna lays her two views beside each other. The wall stays in the same place now.

“The moving wall,” Ronan says.

“It has settled down.”

She smiles and brings out the stair drawing. Her teacher has written a question beside one height. Anna has checked it and added the size.

For the last sheet, she puts two possibilities on the table: the covered yard and the fruit shop.

“Which is clearer?” she asks.

Ronan studies both. He follows the open space in the yard, then looks at the shop baskets.

“I can see the shop more clearly.”

Anna looks at the shutter and nods.

“I want that one too.”

She puts the yard aside and checks the four sheets against the list.

The school accepts hand-drawn copies for this first packet. Anna will keep her originals at home. She starts a fresh copy of the front view. Ronan returns to his own task beside her.

Anna sets the original above the clean page. She checks one corner, then the next, before she begins the window.

Ronan finishes a short answer and looks across.

“Do you have to copy every little line?”

“I need the shape of the building.”

She points to a dark mark at the side of her original.

“Not that one. My pencil slipped there.”

Ronan smiles and moves his own page away from her clean paper.

Anna holds the two drawings side by side for a moment. The new one has only a few lines. It is hard to imagine the finished front yet.

She puts the original back and begins the next corner.

Ronan nearly asks about the stair. He sees her eyes move between the two pages and waits.

He has work of his own. He reads his next question while she draws. They share the quiet table, with enough room for two different tasks.

After a while, he hears her pencil stop.

“Too dark,” she says.

He looks at the heavy roof line. Anna rubs part of it out and starts again with a lighter touch.

Ronan finishes his own page beside her. He closes his book. Anna completes the window on her drawing.

“It takes longer than a form,” he says.

“The form has no roof.”

He laughs quietly. The librarian looks over, and both lower their voices.

Before they leave, Anna copies the deadline into her notebook: the second Friday in November. The packet must reach the school by that day.

The instructions describe a winter review and decisions in the spring afterward. The next class begins in the summer after those decisions.

Anna folds the form back into its envelope. She has work to prepare before she can send it.

Outside, Lin is waiting near the library steps. Anna shows her the four selected drawings. Ronan puts his own book away.

The three walk to the gate together. Ronan carries his book and finished page. Anna holds her drawing folder flat against her arm and tells Lin about the shutter.
studyGuide:
## 词句提示

packet＝一整套材料；original＝原稿；deadline＝截止日期；review＝审阅、审核。

## 理解问题

1. 四张绘图分别是什么？Anna准备寄原稿还是学校允许的手绘副本？
2. 什么时候必须到达？收到表格与清单是否已经等于录取？

## 读句子

**Anna will keep her originals at home.**

拆开看：Anna / will keep / her originals / at home.

Anna／会保留／自己的原稿／放在家中。
